summary: A. P. Buddhadatta (1887–1962) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a tutor in Pali at Ananda College and was attested as a member of Kalyanavamsa Nikaya in 1923.
A. S. Gadre was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He is attested in 1944 as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State and its Archaeology Department.

A. S. Ramanatha Ayyar (d. 1941) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1918–1941), Superintendent in the Travancore State Department of Archaeology (1922), and held a post in Thiruvithamkoor.

A. V. Williams Jackson (1862–1937) was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian studies scholar. He earned his Ph.D. from Columbia and studied at Halle-Wittenberg. At Columbia, he was Adjunct Professor of English Literature (1883–1890) and Professor (1895–1935).
A.-Ferdinand Hérold (1865–1940) was an Indology scholar who studied at the École Nationale des Chartes and the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 1886–1890, earning a Licencié-ès-lettres.
Aalekhya Malladi is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed a PhD at Emory University in 2022. In 2023, Malladi became an Assistant Professor at McGill University.

Aaron P. Proffitt is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He studied at UC Boulder, the IUC, and earned a PhD at the University of Michigan (ca. 2009–2015). He was assistant professor of Japanese Studies at SUNY Albany (~2015–2021).
Abaji Vishnu Kathavate worked in Indology and succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar. He is attested as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2026.

Abanindranath Tagore (1871–1951) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and the Government College of Art and Craft. He held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).

Abdur Rehman is an Indology and archaeology scholar who earned his PhD from the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and studied under Ahmad Hasan Dani. In 1988, he was Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Peshawar.

Abel Bergaigne (1838–1888) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at the EPHE (1868) and the Sorbonne/University of Paris, where he was Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative IE Linguistics (1885).

Abel Hovelacque (1843–1896) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied under Honoré-Joseph Chavée. He served as Professor of Linguistics (1876) and later Director (1891) at the École d'Anthropologie.

Abhijit Mandal is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He earned an MA from Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira (2011–2013) and a Ph.D. from the University of Calcutta (2014–2018), becoming Assistant Professor at Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University in 2016.
Abhimanyu Rao is an Indology scholar who studied under Deepak Dabral and held a post at Shiv Nadar School.

Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra (b. 1943) is an Indologist who studied under Rāmbhadrācārya. He served as head of Sanskrit at Himachal Pradesh University, Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and visiting professor at the University of Indonesia.

Abidin İtil (1910–1980) was an Indologist who studied under Walter Ruben and earned his PhD at Ankara University. He taught Sanskrit there from 1936, served as an assistant (1943–1946), and was Professor and Department Head (~1957–1975).
Abigail I. MacBain is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned an MA at McMaster University (attested 2008) and held a post at the University of Edinburgh in 2022.

Abigail Leach (1855–1918) was a classics and Indology scholar who studied at Radcliffe, Vassar, and Leipzig. She taught at Boston Latin Academy (1880–1883), became Head of Greek at Vassar (1889), and served as President of the SCS (1898–1900).

Abirlal Gangopadhyay is an Indologist who studied at Ramakrishna Math Vivekananda Veda Vidyalaya, Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute, Jadavpur University (MA, 2016–2018), and the University of Hyderabad, where he earned a PhD (2018–2023).

Abraham Anthony Fokker (1862–1927) was a linguist who earned a Ph.D. at Leiden University (~1889–1894). He served as a professor at the University of Indonesia and taught Malay at the University of Amsterdam (~1919–1927).
